title: ARISE: Augmented-Reality Intervention with Action Preview and Spatial Editing for Robot Policy Adaptation
abstract_latex: Imitation learning policies usually suffer from covariate shift at deployment---the policy-induced state distribution might drift from the expert training distribution, causing unexpected failures. Human corrections at learner-visited states can help adapt the policy. Traditional takeover-based human intervention, however, often reveals errors only after they unfold and can force operators to replace the policy's predicted actions. We present \sys{}, a policy-aware augmented-reality human-in-the-loop correction system that, after each policy inference, renders the active action chunk as a spatially registered end-effector trajectory. Before execution resumes, an operator can drag a future waypoint to locally edit the predicted actions. These edits yield executed corrections for data-efficient policy fine-tuning (FT for short) and aligned original--corrected action pairs that support a compact residual predictor over a frozen base policy, enabling parameter-efficient adaptation. Across three real-robot tasks, including long-horizon and precise manipulation tasks, \sys{} improves mean task success from 10.6\% for the base policies to 91.9\% with finetuning and 85.3\% with residual adaptation within two policy-update rounds. \sys{} makes policy predictions observable and editable, providing a direct interface for corrective robot policy adaptation.
